source.title: Sensitivity and Generalization in Neural Networks: an Empirical Study
source.authors: Roman Novak; Yasaman Bahri; Daniel A. Abolafia; Jeffrey Pennington; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: Compares fully connected networks trained on true versus random CIFAR-10 labels and reports their training accuracy and generalization gap, conceptually testing whether fitting random labels rules out generalization on natural labels.
record.gate_note: Figure 4 reports paired comparisons across many hyperparameter configurations, not per-network numeric values. The text says both label conditions reached 100% training accuracy; the plotted values are figure-only. Other reported experiments compare data augmentation, activation functions, and full-batch versus mini-batch optimization, but do not test the specific claim versions about adaptive optimizers, large-batch budgets, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: Matched fully connected networks trained with true or random CIFAR-10 labels both reach 100% training accuracy, and the authors report better generalization with true labels. This tests V1's coexistence finding, although the supplied text does not establish chance-level random-label test accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the label comparison but understates the paper's main conclusion: input-output Jacobian sensitivity predicts generalization across many image-classification settings, depends strongly on proximity to the data manifold, and can remain informative at individual test points.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fully connected networks on cropped CIFAR10 and compares true versus random labels while measuring generalization gaps; the named V1 examples and recipes are not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that sensitivity and generalization change together when labels, data augmentation, activation function, or optimization procedure change; the reported label comparison is across varied network hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Among 2160 CIFAR-10 networks with 100% training accuracy, a model with maximum parameter count generalizes best; its parameter count is approximately 10^4 times that of the smallest fitting model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across the sampled architectures and training configurations, extremely overparameterized networks can generalize better than smaller networks that also fit the training data. This does not isolate widening as required by V2.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-output Jacobian norm correlates with generalization across the tested image datasets, while transition count does not generally compare networks of different sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average sensitivity to input perturbations correlates with generalization in the tested fully connected networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Correct labels, augmentation, ReLU activations, and mini-batch momentum training rather than full-batch L-BFGS improve generalization and reduce Jacobian sensitivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several architectural and training choices that improve generalization also reduce input sensitivity; the optimizer comparison does not isolate batch size.

record.problems: Figure 4 result values are only plotted, with no numerical values recoverable from the supplied text. The large experiment sampled configurations unevenly, with small models more likely to be evaluated, and Figure 4's generalization results are described for selected paired networks that reached 100% training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Other Figure 4 comparisons and the broad sensitivity-versus-gap sweeps are not separate rows for the claim versions tested here; they concern different claim aspects or measures and are summarized under gate_note and fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels is not established by the supplied text. The named convolutional architectures and ImageNet setting are not tested.
A controlled width comparison beyond interpolation is not reported. Figure 1 varies parameter count across architectures and training configurations.
Adaptive optimizers occur in the sweep, but no adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance comparison under the specified tuning conditions is reported.
No batch-size comparison holding optimizer and epoch budget fixed; the plotted comparison changes both optimizer and batch size.
Input-output Jacobian sensitivity is measured, rather than magnitude-scaled sensitivity to weight perturbations.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The paired analysis selects configurations that fit both conditions perfectly; it does not estimate how often arbitrary configurations achieve this. No scope penalty follows merely from testing fully connected networks on CIFAR-10.

versions.untested_parts: The specific small Inception, AlexNet and MLP architectures; ImageNet/Inception V3; and the Zhang et al. 2017 recipes and measurements.

rows.note: Authors state the generalization improvement from using correct labels is coupled with reduced sensitivity; Figure 4 plots the true-label and random-label gaps without recoverable numerical values.
rows.check: Perfect random-label training fit is explicitly established, but the supplied figure text does not establish that held-out accuracy is at chance. The architecture range lost superscripts: maximum width is 2^16 and maximum depth is 2^6 + 1. Uncertainty is reported as standard errors, usually across eight seeds, rather than unstated.

relationships.condition: Selected matched fully connected CIFAR-10 configurations reaching 100% training accuracy with both true and random labels
relationships.reason: R1–R2 establish perfect fitting in both conditions, and Figure 4 explicitly reports improved generalization with true labels. This supports coexistence; chance-level random-label test accuracy remains unverified.
relationships.display_finding: The reported perfect fitting under both labelings and improved natural-label generalization remain unverified from the available source.
